audit.why: 51.79% over 1450 games at diff 8.5/10. The rating looks high against a winning record, but it is right: the lane is genuinely hard and the win rate comes from levels 6 onward, which is exactly what the corrected chart now says.

audit.whatIsWrong: SIX of seven level-chart rows disagree with the packet chart, and every one of them contradicts its own why-text. Packet is [Teemo, Skill, Skill, Teemo, Riven, Riven, Skill]; both layers hold [Teemo, Teemo, Teemo, Skill, Teemo, Skill, Teemo].
audit.why: whys[1] says Level 2 trades 'become close to even' under win[1]=Teemo. whys[2] says 'genuinely 50-50' under win[2]=Teemo. whys[3] says 'he edges this window' under win[3]=Skill. whys[4] calls Level 6 'your clearest kill window' under win[4]=Teemo. whys[5] says 'force the all-in now' under win[5]=Skill. whys[6] opens 'You win the straight 1v1' under win[6]=Teemo. As shipped, the chart says Teemo wins five rows on a page whose prose says he wins one.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 6 -> Skill; row 3 -> Teemo; rows 4, 5 -> Riven, in both layers, all six ratings re-pointed, phases[6].why rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entire page is built on tracking Blinding Dart, and both places that give a number give a different wrong one: whys[1] says 'roughly 10-second cooldown at rank 1', content.early says 'count to four seconds'.
audit.why: Blinding Dart is 7 SECONDS FLAT at every rank. Ten seconds means the player stands there through three free autos after the window already opened; four seconds means they walk in while it is still up and lose the trade outright. One number, wrong in both directions, on the one cooldown the matchup is named after.
audit.corrected: Both corrected to 7 seconds flat, with the count-to-seven instruction that follows from it.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] says the blind makes 'your W and Q autos deal zero damage'. The full layer gets this right ('Blinds autos — not your W or Q') and the content layer contradicts it. Separately, Move Quick's counterplay appears nowhere: whys[3], spikes[0], wants.foe[1] and content.early all treat his move speed as an unanswerable kite.
audit.why: Blind stops basic attacks only. Broken Wings, Ki Burst, Valor and Wind Slash all land at full damage through it — the cost is that the Runic Blade charges you stacked go unspent, which the mirror identified from the other side. And Riot's W text: Move Quick 'passively increas[es] his Move Speed UNTIL HE IS STRUCK by an enemy champion or turret'. Landing any part of your Q chain strips the passive outright. The single hit that starts your combo is also the hit that ends the kite.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[0] restated onto the Runic Blade charge loss; the Move Quick strip written into content.early.
sources: mirrorFindings point 4 (blinded auto / Runic Blade charges)

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid states 'Wind Slash at 40-50% HP executes through his poison' — an invented health threshold.
audit.why: The mirror killed this exact fabrication on another Riven page: Wind Slash scales with the target's MISSING health and has no threshold at all. A stated percentage tells the player to wait for a number that does not exist, which either wastes the window or holds a 120-second ultimate through the fight it was meant to end.
audit.corrected: content.mid and wants.you[2] restated as scaling with missing health, no threshold.
sources: mirrorFindings point 4 (Wind Slash scales with missing health, no threshold)

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid-game section credits the 4-5 window to nothing in particular.
audit.why: The mirror established the real shape: Broken Wings is 13 seconds at EVERY rank, so the levelling spike at 4-5 is Ki Burst reaching 9 and Valor reaching 8. That is the concrete reason your combo density improves while his poison ramps.

edits.before: His Q blind is on a roughly 10-second cooldown at rank 1 — if you watch it and step up only when it expires, Level 2 trades become close to even.
edits.after: Blinding Dart is 7 seconds flat at every rank — count seven from his cast and step up on the seventh, and Level 2 trades come out close to even.

edits.before: Teemo owns Level 1 hard — his auto-range means he can poke you for free before you have W online, and every attempt to walk up with a Q is a blind (Q) invitation that silences your autos and makes the trade a net loss for you. Last-hit at the very tip of Q range and accept a few poison stacks rather than burning E just to get blinded. At Level 2 you have W but he now has his full kite toolkit — only step up if his Q blind is visibly on cooldown (watch for the CD icon or count to four seconds), then E in immediately and W-stun before his passive move-speed pulls him away. At Level 3 the math evens out: your full Q-W-E combo can burst him in one rotation if the blind is down, but if he lands Q first your whole window evaporates — the lane is genuinely coin-flip based on who times the blind correctly.
edits.after: Teemo owns Level 1 hard — his auto-range means he pokes you for free before you have W online, and every walk-up is a Blinding Dart invitation that shuts off your autos and makes the trade a net loss. Last-hit at the very tip of Q range and accept a few poison stacks rather than burning E just to get blinded. At Level 2 you have W but he has his full kite toolkit — Blinding Dart is 7 seconds flat at every rank, so count seven from his cast, step up on the seventh, then E in and W-stun. Move Quick's passive speed drops the instant any of your damage strikes him, so the first Q hit is what stops the kite. At Level 3 the maths evens: your full Q-W-E combo bursts him in one rotation if the blind is down, but if he lands it first your window evaporates — coin-flip on who times the dart.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 tilt back to Teemo because his poison damage ramps and your sustain has not completed yet — without Shieldbow's shield and lifesteal you are eating too much to reliably all-in even on his blind cooldown. Play the wave rather than the 1v1: shove, back, and try to return with Serrated Dirk or Pickaxe to shift the damage equation. At Level 6 the lane flips in your favour: Blade of the Exile gives you enough extra range that E-W-Q1-Q2-R(first cast)-Q3-Wind Slash can kill him from slightly beyond his auto range, and Wind Slash at 40-50% HP executes through his poison without requiring you to survive a prolonged chase. Force the Level 6 all-in the moment he overextends past the midpoint of the lane — if he is standing near his tower you cannot safely follow.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 tilt back to Teemo because his poison ramps and your sustain has not completed — without Shieldbow's shield and lifesteal you eat too much to all-in reliably even on his blind cooldown. What does improve is your own kit: Broken Wings stays 13 seconds at every rank, but Ki Burst reaches 9 here and Valor reaches 8. Play the wave rather than the 1v1: shove, back, return with a Pickaxe to shift the damage equation. At Level 6 the lane flips: Blade of the Exile gives enough range that E-W-Q1-Q2-R-Q3-Wind Slash kills from beyond his auto range, and Wind Slash scales with the health he is already missing — there is no threshold to wait for. Force it the moment he steps past the lane midpoint; near his tower you cannot follow.

edits.after: Reach Level 6 with a health lead so Wind Slash lands on a Teemo already missing health — it scales, it does not threshold
